head: One rookie.
Almost the whole budget.
slides.sub: How Nike bet its basketball future on a player who had never played a pro game.

image.label: A lone basketball player silhouetted in an empty arena
image.brief: 1980년대 텅 빈 실내 농구 경기장, 천장 조명 하나 아래 서 있는 농구 선수의 실루엣. 얼굴은 보이지 않음. 긴장감 있는 영화 같은 톤. 실제 로고 없음.

head: Nike in 1984:
losing its stride.
body: Nike had grown on the running boom of the 1970s. By 1984, profits were falling and the company was cutting jobs.
The hot new shoe was Reebok's aerobics sneaker, and Nike had missed it.

image.label: A quiet 1980s sneaker office with stacks of shoe boxes
image.brief: 1980년대 미국 오리건의 신발 회사 사무실. 쌓인 신발 상자, 조용한 책상들, 흐린 창밖. 침체된 분위기. 브랜드 로고 없음.

head: On the court,
Nike was an extra.
body: Basketball belonged to Converse and Adidas. Nike paid many NBA players small sums to wear its shoes, but no one remembered which players wore what.
The money was spread so thin it bought almost nothing.

image.label: Rows of generic white high-top sneakers in a locker room
image.brief: 1980년대 NBA 라커룸 바닥에 늘어선 비슷비슷한 흰색 하이톱 운동화들. 특징 없는 느낌. 실제 브랜드 디자인 없음.

head: A rookie who
wanted Adidas.
body: Michael Jordan was the third pick in the 1984 draft. Reportedly, he wanted to sign with Adidas and barely wanted to visit Nike.
A story often told: Nike adviser Sonny Vaccaro urged the company to put its basketball money on Jordan alone.

image.label: A young player's silhouette at a meeting table with sneaker sketches
image.brief: 회의실 탁자에 놓인 운동화 스케치들 앞에 앉은 젊은 선수의 뒷모습 실루엣. 1980년대 미국 사무실. 실존 인물 얼굴 없음.

head: Profits are falling.
Where does the money go?
body: You run Nike's basketball business. Your budget is limited, and your brand is invisible on the court.

options.text: Keep paying many players modest deals to spread the risk
options.feedback: Safe if one player gets hurt or flops. But it's the plan that already wasn't working. Keep swiping.

options.text: Cut back on basketball and chase aerobics like Reebok
options.feedback: That's where the sales were growing. You'd be a late follower in someone else's market. Keep swiping.

options.text: Put most of it on one rookie and give him his own shoe
options.feedback: Huge upside, but a rookie with no pro games could fail or get injured. Keep swiping.

image.label: Stacks of money split between many shoes or one shoe
image.brief: 탁자 위 돈다발을 여러 켤레 운동화에 나눠 놓을지 한 켤레에 몰아 놓을지 보여주는 상징적 구도. 1980년대 색감.

slides.label: Jordan's five-year deal, reportedly, plus a share of sales
body: Nike went all in. Jordan got a signature shoe, the Air Jordan, and royalties on every pair. For a player who had not played a single NBA game, that was almost unheard of.

image.label: A contract and a pen beside a red and black sneaker
image.brief: 계약서와 펜 옆에 놓인 빨강·검정 하이톱 운동화. 실제 Air Jordan 디자인이나 로고는 따라 하지 않음.

head: The league said no.
Nike said thanks.
body: The NBA objected that his black-and-red shoes broke its uniform rules.
Nike turned the complaint into an ad: the league had banned them, but it couldn't stop you from wearing them. A rule became the best marketing Nike had.

image.label: A sneaker on a TV screen with a black bar across it
image.brief: 1980년대 브라운관 TV 화면 속 운동화에 검은 막대가 가로질러 있는 장면. 거실 분위기. 로고 없음.

slides.label: Air Jordan sales in the first year, reportedly
body: Jordan won Rookie of the Year, and kids lined up for his shoes in 1985. The bet paid back many times over, far beyond what Nike had hoped for.

image.label: Kids lining up outside a 1980s sneaker store
image.brief: 1985년 미국 쇼핑몰 신발 가게 앞에 줄 선 아이들과 청소년들. 따뜻한 오후 빛. 간판에 실제 상표 없음.

head: A shoe that became
a brand of its own.
body: Nike kept making a new Air Jordan nearly every year. The line grew into its own brand inside Nike, now worth billions of dollars a year.
Far more of its fans buy the shoes than play basketball.

image.label: A wall of sneakers in many colors in a modern store
image.brief: 현대 매장 벽면을 채운 다양한 색의 하이톱 운동화들. 실제 로고나 실제 모델 디자인 없음.

head: Small bets stay small.
Focus makes a brand.
body: Spreading money across many players looked safe, but each deal was too small to matter. The expected value of one big, focused bet was far higher, even with the risk.
One star, one shoe, one story gave Nike something rivals couldn't copy.

image.label: One spotlight on a single sneaker among many in shadow
image.brief: 어둠 속 여러 운동화 가운데 한 켤레에만 스포트라이트가 비치는 장면.

head: Spread too thin,
nobody notices you.
body: When resources are tight, many small bets can feel safe and still add up to nothing.
**Try it today:** list where your marketing or time is spread thin. Which one bet would you back fully?

image.label: A single basketball resting on a court at dusk
image.brief: 해 질 녘 야외 농구 코트에 놓인 농구공 하나. 따뜻한 빛과 긴 그림자.

factChecks.note: 1984년 무렵 Nike의 이익 감소와 감원, Reebok 에어로빅화의 급성장은 Phil Knight의 회고록 『Shoe Dog』(2016)과 당시 보도로 확인하세요. 카드에는 구체적인 수치를 넣지 않았습니다.
Jordan이 1984 NBA 드래프트에서 Chicago Bulls에 전체 3순위로 지명된 사실과 1984~85 시즌 신인상 수상은 NBA 공식 기록으로 확인하세요.
Jordan이 원래 Adidas를 선호했고 어머니의 권유로 Nike 미팅에 갔다는 이야기, Sonny Vaccaro가 농구 예산을 한 선수에게 모으자고 주장했다는 이야기는 널리 전해지는 내용이라 "reportedly", "a story often told"로 표시했습니다.
계약 조건 "5년 약 250만 달러(연 약 50만 달러)와 로열티"는 여러 언론 보도 기준입니다. 자료마다 세부 조건이 다르므로 카드에 "reportedly"로 표시했습니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] 1984년 10월 26일 5년 250만 달러와 로열티 계약 확인.
NBA가 흑·적색 신발이 유니폼 규정에 어긋난다며 문제를 삼았고 Nike가 이를 'Banned' 광고로 활용한 것은 사실입니다. 다만 실제로 문제가 된 신발은 Air Jordan 1이 아니라 Air Ship이었다는 보도가 있어, 카드에는 "his black-and-red shoes"로만 적고 벌금 액수는 넣지 않았습니다.
Air Jordan 첫해 매출 "1억 달러 이상"은 널리 인용되는 수치(흔히 약 1억 2,600만 달러)이지만 공식 공시 여부를 확인하세요. 카드에는 "more than $100 million"과 "reportedly"로 적었습니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] 첫해 1억 2,600만 달러 보도 확인(논란 표시 있음, 'reportedly' 유지).
Jordan 브랜드가 현재 연간 수십억 달러 규모라는 표현은 Nike 연례보고서의 Jordan Brand 매출로 확인하세요. 카드에는 "billions of dollars a year"로만 적었습니다.
